Description: As the product owner, I want the method tested on real learners before building, so that the design is proven.
Acceptance criteria: 5+ learners tested; 4+ can name the finger for E, R and O after Orient; findings report written

Description: As the product owner, I want a hands-on comparison, so that we know where EyesUp must be better.
Acceptance criteria: Five tools used for 30+ min each; table of strengths and gaps

Summary: English word list and letter model
Description: As a learner, I want practice words that feel natural, so that drills transfer to real typing.
Acceptance criteria: 10,000-word list with licence in SOURCES.md; order-3 letter model; blocklist applied

Summary: Engine spike: lines from unlocked keys
Description: As a developer, I want a proof that line generation works, so that Phase 1 starts on solid ground.
Acceptance criteria: Given unlocked keys, generator returns lines using only those keys with focus key at 25-35%

Description: As a developer, I want to see raw key events on each OS, so that input risks surface early.
Acceptance criteria: Page logs code, key, timeStamp, repeat, modifiers, keyup; run on Windows, macOS, Ubuntu

Description: As a developer, I want the repo, CI and checks in place, so that every change is tested.
Acceptance criteria: pnpm workspace builds; CI runs unit tests, e2e and validate-layouts on every PR

Description: As a new learner, I want a few quick questions, so that EyesUp starts where I am.
Acceptance criteria: One question per screen; keys 1-4 pick, Enter continues; answers saved

Description: As a new learner, I want to type normally for 45 seconds, so that my everyday speed is known.
Acceptance criteria: 45 s timer; net WPM and accuracy saved as baseline; layout fingerprinted

Summary: Probe B: home-position check and blind lines
Description: As a new learner, I want a short blind test, so that EyesUp knows what my fingers already know.
Acceptance criteria: 4 home prompts scored 0-4; home-row line and 20 s word line with keyboard hidden

Description: As a new learner, I want to see my track and why, so that I trust where I start.
Acceptance criteria: Rules match the plan on 10 scripted profiles; reason shown; override in one tap

Description: As a learner with a non-US keyboard, I want to confirm my layout, so that the keyboard on screen matches mine.
Acceptance criteria: Detected layout shown; change opens layout list; choice saved

Description: As a learner, I want every key I press read correctly, so that my scores are fair.
Acceptance criteria: Drops repeats; holds dead keys; reads AltGr and Caps Lock; pauses scoring during IME; K01-K08 pass in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit

Summary: Mastery model: key and pair confidence
Description: As a learner, I want practice to target my weakest keys, so that I improve fastest.
Acceptance criteria: Confidence formula from the plan; unit tests for unlock and focus-key selection

Summary: Text generator: pseudo-words and real words
Description: As a learner, I want lines built from keys I know, so that I'm never asked to type unknown keys.
Acceptance criteria: Only unlocked keys; focus key in every word; blocklist test passes on 10,000 generated lines

Description: As a learner, I want each session planned for me, so that I just press Enter and practise.
Acceptance criteria: Warm-up, new keys, mixed review, words, blind check every third session; sizes match daily minutes

Description: As a learner, I want old keys to come back now and then, so that I don't forget them.
Acceptance criteria: Review interval doubles per stable session up to 30 days; resets on a slip

Description: As a learner, I want to see what I've typed and what's next, so that I can keep my eyes on the text.
Acceptance criteria: Per-character render; caret; errors tinted; keystroke-to-paint under 16 ms p95

Description: As a learner, I want the keyboard guide to fade as I improve, so that I stop depending on it.
Acceptance criteria: Draws any layout file; levels L0-L3 per key; steps up and back by the plan's rules

Description: As a beginner, I want to see which finger moves where, so that I learn the right movement.
Acceptance criteria: Hands at rest; 400 ms reach for keys at L0; static arrow with reduced motion

Description: As a learner, I want to peek when stuck, so that I can continue without looking down.
Acceptance criteria: Full keyboard while Ctrl held; peeked keystrokes logged as guided

Description: As a learner, I want the timer to stop when I'm interrupted, so that my speed is honest.
Acceptance criteria: Esc, blur and hidden tab pause; resume with Esc; idle time excluded

Description: As a beginner, I want the line to wait for the right key, so that I never practise a wrong movement.
Acceptance criteria: Stop-on-error for Foundations; mark-and-continue for others; Backspace off in drills

Description: As a learner, I want to start from the home row every time, so that my fingers find their place.
Acceptance criteria: Session starts when F and J are pressed together (K18)

Summary: Line result strip and session summary
Description: As a learner, I want to see what changed, so that I know I'm improving.
Acceptance criteria: Strip after each line; summary lists guide changes, slowest pairs, crossover progress

Description: As a learner, I want to see a new key's movement before typing it, so that I learn it right first time.
Acceptance criteria: Card with reach animation for each new key; replay with Tab; Enter starts the drill

Description: As a learner, I want a reminder to rest, so that my hands don't get sore.
Acceptance criteria: After 20 min of typing, 30 s stretch card; skip with Enter

Description: As a learner, I want one obvious next step each day, so that practising is effortless.
Acceptance criteria: Start session with Enter; streak survives one rest day a week; next keys shown

Description: As a learner, I want my progress saved and exportable, so that I never lose it.
Acceptance criteria: Saved after every line; JSON export and delete-everything in settings

Description: As a learner, I want EyesUp to work without internet, so that I can practise anywhere.
Acceptance criteria: Service worker caches app and content; all learning works offline (NFR-05)

Summary: Display settings: text size, contrast, dark, reduced motion
Description: As a learner with different needs, I want to adjust the display, so that I can practise comfortably.
Acceptance criteria: Settings persist; dark tokens applied; reduced motion swaps animations

Description: As a self-taught looker, I want to see when blind typing will beat my old speed, so that I stay with it.
Acceptance criteria: Crossover chart from day 1; dip explainer card; projected session from last 10 sessions

Description: As a Retrain learner, I want a structured switch to everyday touch typing, so that the habit sticks.
Acceptance criteria: Opt-in at 25 WPM blind with all letters; 7 daily check-ins; L3 keystrokes worth 4x L0

Description: As a fluent typist, I want drills on my slowest pairs and rhythm, so that I get past my plateau.
Acceptance criteria: Slow-pair drills; metronome; rollover drills; timed tests

Description: As a developer, I want to practise symbols and real code, so that I stop looking for brackets.
Acceptance criteria: Snippets per language; brackets and operators unlocked by the overlay

Description: As a data-entry worker, I want number drills, so that I type figures blind.
Acceptance criteria: Number-row drills; keypad lessons on full-size keyboards (K17)

Description: As a French-speaking learner, I want my keyboard and language, so that practice matches my daily typing.
Acceptance criteria: azerty-fr.json live; French word list, model and phrases; dead keys pass K04

Description: As a learner, I want to see every key's progress, so that I know what to work on.
Acceptance criteria: Heatmap with numbers on hover; speed and accuracy history; milestones list

Description: As a learner, I want to race my own best run, so that practice feels like a game without strangers.
Acceptance criteria: Ghost caret replays best run on the same text

Description: As a learner, I want to practise on my own emails and code, so that skills transfer to real work.
Acceptance criteria: Paste, save, practise; text never leaves the device; locked keys shown with full guide

Summary: One-hand and reduced-finger maps; dyslexia-friendly text
Description: As a learner with a disability, I want a finger map that fits me, so that I can learn too.
Acceptance criteria: Alternate finger maps selectable; dyslexia-friendly font and spacing option

Summary: Keyboard-less device screen and public site
Description: As a phone visitor, I want to understand EyesUp and get the link to a computer, so that I can start later.
Acceptance criteria: Touch-first device with no key press shows the hand-off screen; public site readable at 390 px

Description: As a desktop learner, I want the same app with local storage, so that it works offline from first launch.
Acceptance criteria: Web build runs in Tauri on all three OSes; SQLite schema v1; storage adapter passes the same tests

Summary: Import web export on first launch
Description: As a learner moving to desktop, I want my progress to come with me, so that I don't start over.
Acceptance criteria: Open an export file; all keys, sessions and texts imported; duplicates skipped

Description: As a learner on any OS, I want a normal installer, so that setup is easy.
Acceptance criteria: MSI, NSIS, universal DMG, .deb, .rpm, AppImage, Flatpak built in CI

Description: As a learner, I want the app to install without security warnings, so that I trust it.
Acceptance criteria: Windows Authenticode; macOS Developer ID + notarization; GPG for Linux

Description: As a learner, I want updates to arrive safely, so that I always have fixes.
Acceptance criteria: Signed manifest; update offered between sessions only; tampered update refused

Description: As a learner, I want an optional daily nudge, so that I keep my rhythm.
Acceptance criteria: Off by default; one per day at the chosen time; none on rest days

Description: As a learner, I want EyesUp to reopen as I left it, so that I start practising at once.
Acceptance criteria: Size and position remembered; full-screen toggle in practice

Summary: Keyboard matrix sign-off and store submissions
Description: As the product owner, I want proof input works everywhere, so that we can release.
Acceptance criteria: Every applicable K01-K18 cell passes on all environments; Microsoft Store and Flathub submitted

Description: As a new learner, I want a short welcome and Orient lesson, so that I start with posture and finger zones.
Acceptance criteria: Welcome starts with Enter and needs no account. Orient teaches posture, home position, the F and J bumps and finger zones in about 4 minutes. A learner can name the finger for E, R and O afterwards. Orient can be replayed from Library. Keyboard-only throughout.

Description: As a learner, I want to change layout, track and goal and export my data, so that EyesUp fits how I type.
Acceptance criteria: Change layout, track and goal; access profile; sound; JSON export; delete everything with confirmation. Key progress is kept when the track changes.

Description: As the product owner, I want Gate B numbers from learner JSON exports, so that we can decide the next phase.
Acceptance criteria: A zero-dependency Node script reads a folder of learner JSON exports and prints the Gate B numbers and the supporting metrics, with no text content and no keystroke logs in its output.

Description: As a learner, I want to select an advanced Fire Typing Game mode, so that practice can feel like a high-energy game without leaving the app.
Acceptance criteria: Learner can select Fire Typing Game from a mode control; game-style practice remains on-device only (no typed text or keystroke timing leaves the device); out of Phases 0–3 scope until Gate B and an explicit product-owner go.
